method: Rebuilt the Amsterdam study-unit buckets directly from current EER Table 1 and compared them with the VU curriculum. Reconsidered the choice of Humane by Design and its module-eight unit, progression and the final project before checking the exact UCR schedules, contributions and reader fields.
findings: The 2026–2027 EEMCS Creative Technology EER, section B Article 1.2 Table 1, and the current VU curriculum establish the English-taught Amsterdam location of the joint UT–VU degree. Eight mandatory module slots total 120 EC. Humane by Design is the Amsterdam-delivered module-five choice; the other choices are available at UT. The example retains the location-representative choice independently of UCR fit. The 15 EC module includes a core (3.5 EC), Utopia and Designing Futures Project (6 EC), Fairness in Data Science (5 EC), and professional development (0.5 EC). The associated module-eight choice is Dangerous Design (2.5 EC). Year three has a 30 EC approved minor or exchange and a graduation semester with Academic Writing (5 EC), Reflection (5 EC), and two project parts (5 and 15 EC). The 12 reader components preserve coherent modules; the study-unit list records their individual weights.

EER B1.8 requires 60 year-one and 30 year-two EC before minor study. Module 11 non-project study units require 60 year-one and 45 year-two EC. Graduation Project normally requires all 120 EC of modules 1–8, with limited pending-result and dispensation provisions. The second project part follows completion of the first. The EER also bars concurrent major projects across modules. The standard sequential route satisfies these conditions. The minor is genuine approved space with restrictions on internships, external courses, overlap and project participation. The final design assignment uses a public presentation and defence.

The smart option uses actual signal analysis and computational robotics, while sensor work, circuits and installation projects remain distinct. Humane by Design provides a partial comparison with AI Ethics through fairness and social impacts, and the standalone Academic Writing unit relates to the UCR rhetoric course through written argument. General Ethics remains a contribution to the UCR options, with the graduation reflection unit separately visible. Creative Communication Laboratory supports a limited relationship with Art, Impact and Technology through deliberate artistic choices and audience experience. Consumer Product Design supports a direct but bounded relationship with Interaction Design through user needs, prototyping and iterative testing. Qualitative and empirical methods support the human option without claiming the full UX studio. The official project is individual and compulsory; the 15 EC optional UCR element is outside each planned 180 EC.
